reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Commonest intracranial complication of otitis media is meningitis
Picket fence fever means lateral sinus thrombophlebitis
Gradenigo triad: otorrhoea, retro-orbital pain, abducens palsy
reference.pathophysiology: Infection breaches thin tegmen, sinus plates and labyrinthine windows directly or via thrombophlebitic emissary veins, seeding meninges, brain parenchyma and venous sinuses from the infected mastoid reservoir.
additionalDifferentials: Otogenic versus rhinogenic brain abscess site clues
Labyrinthitis (deaf vertigo) versus benign positional vertigo
additionalInvestigations: CT temporal bone with contrast; MRI brain when intracranial signs
Lumbar puncture only after imaging clearance
